chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited to me the inheritance laws (Faraid) of Ali (peace be upon him), and among them is: 'The husband acquires the entire estate if there is no other heir.'
ai.seo_question: What is the husband's share of inheritance if the wife has no other heirs?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the continuity of legal tradition by linking the inheritance rulings of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) directly to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), underscoring the authenticity of the 'Faraid Ali' corpus in Shia jurisprudence. The specific ruling that a husband inherits the entire estate in the absence of other heirs reflects the principle of *al-ghalib* (the dominant heir) when no closer relatives or fixed-share heirs exist, a concept central to Shia inheritance law.
